kind: resident wireframe preparation/software/GPU-submission CPU and memory diagnostic
methodology: Identical release probe source and dependency locks with exact locked sotf-wgpu git source; separate baseline/candidate targets. GPU feature is required in both builds; candidate feature enables GPU wire cases unavailable on baseline. Allocator-disabled ABBA twice, four fresh processes/version, one warmup and five samples/case; separate allocator-instrumented builds. No task-owned build/check/test processes ran during timing. CPU uses aggregate CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID. Preparation creates a fresh Scene/cache per invocation and returns owner plus PreparedScene for checks/destruction outside timing. Software frames retain preparation, time frame allocation/rasterization including wire drawing, and check exact within-version pixels and geometry_builds==1. GPU submission times the public render API: encoder creation, uniform staging, draw encoding and queue submit, with resident geometry. Target/device/upload/initial warm rendering, GPU completion, readback, pixel checks and output destruction are excluded. Readback waits for each fresh submitted frame outside timing. These GPU numbers are CPU submission costs, not GPU execution latency or throughput. Wire-off software/GPU image hashes must match baseline exactly. Baseline software silently ignores requested wires; baseline GPU rejects them, so candidate GPU wire-on cases compare against baseline wire-off only as an overhead reference, not equivalent semantics. Independent wireframe integration qualifies edges/alpha/clipping/occlusion. Grids 8/24/48 cubed, 128-square frames, plus software 24-cubed at 512 square; opaque and half-opacity viridis fields. Baseline 28 cases, candidate 34. Single default preparation chunk per fixture, so cross-chunk ownership is qualified by tests rather than these timings. Payload means retained derived scene bytes for preparation/software and actual uploaded geometry buffers for GPU; canonical source, targets, LUTs/uniforms, metadata and allocator overhead are excluded. Allocation bytes include positive realloc growth, not entire resized-buffer traffic or peak/live/RSS. Shared host without controlled affinity/thermal state. No energy, mobile, whole-application or other-device qualification claim.
